source: General US patterns for how property passes at death: beneficiary designations and payable-on-death forms first, joint title next, then a will, and the state's intestacy rules when there is none. Not legal advice; the details vary by state and by account.
confidenceNote: Widely described conventions, not statute. Which route a given asset takes depends on how the account is set up and on the state; this table maps each category to the route it usually takes when nothing special has been done.
note: what passes by beneficiary, by will, or by the state

routes.label: By beneficiary designation
routes.note: The form on the account decides. It overrides the will.

routes.label: By title
routes.note: Property held jointly with right of survivorship passes to the co-owner by the deed or the account title, not the will.

routes.label: By will
routes.note: Whatever has no designation and no joint title goes through the will, and through probate.

routes.label: By the state's rules
routes.note: With no will, the state's intestacy rules decide who gets what would have passed by will; with no beneficiary named, the designated accounts usually fall back to the estate and take the same road.

categories.label: Cash & savings
categories.note: A payable-on-death (POD) designation on a bank account passes it straight to the person named. Without one it falls into the estate.

categories.label: Brokerage & taxable
categories.note: A plain brokerage account has no beneficiary unless a transfer-on-death registration was added; by default it passes by will.

categories.label: Retirement accounts
categories.note: 401(k)s and IRAs pass by the beneficiary form on file with the plan, whatever the will says. A workplace plan's form usually names the spouse by law unless waived.

categories.label: Property
categories.note: Solely held property passes by will. Property held jointly with right of survivorship passes by title to the co-owner instead; assets here carry no title flag, so it is counted as solely held.

categories.label: Vehicles
categories.note: A vehicle in one name passes by will; some states allow a transfer-on-death registration on the title.

categories.label: Everything else
categories.note: Anything with no designation and no joint title goes through the will.

documents.will: A will says who gets what passes through your estate, and who settles it; without one the state's rules decide.
documents.beneficiaries: A beneficiary form on each retirement account, life-insurance policy and payable-on-death bank account passes that money directly, ahead of the will.
documents.poa: A power of attorney names someone to act for you — pay bills, sign, decide — while you are alive but cannot; it ends at death.

guardian: A will is also where a guardian for minor children is named. Without one, a court chooses.
lifeInsurance: Life insurance passes by its beneficiary form too; it is not an asset in this model, so it is not counted here.
